transcript.answer: No, not any more. ADR-039 originally decided that review-type agents would be pinned to a different model family from the implementer. The setup was an Anthropic implementer with an OpenAI reviewer, or the reverse. Under that decision the settings UI warned when both resolved to the same family. An amendment dated 2026-10-14 reverses this. `code-review` and `code-review-recheck` now run on `gemini-4-argon`, which is the same family as the implementation loop's `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`. The amendment says cross-family review "is no longer a rule, only one input to the model choice". It gives a bench result as the reason: Argon found all five known must-fixes that finished (one timed out), against four of six for Sonnet. The cost is about three times slower reviews and about 40% higher spend. I did not read the full text of the amendment or of PR #1091, so there may be details I missed.

judgements.reason: The answer states that ADR-039 made cross-family review the rule and that the 2026-10-14 amendment moved code-review and code-review-recheck to gemini-4-argon, the implementer's own family, because it caught more, leaving cross-family as only one input; it does not contradict the gold answer.
